reports.title: Aramark Reports Earnings Results for Fiscal 2026

guidance.heading: OUTLOOK
section: Aramark currently anticipates its full-year financial performance for fiscal 2027 as follows:

“Our teams remain focused on delivering for our clients and building on the success throughout the business,” Zillmer added. “With multiple, broad-based growth drivers already underway, I couldn't be more excited about the significant opportunities ahead.”

desk.headline: Q4 revenue up 5% to $5.29bn, in line; adjusted EPS of $0.71 misses; FY27 outlook targets 20–25% EPS growth

other.label: Organic revenue growth
other.change: Q4; about 2 points from calendar shift

results: Q4 revenue rose 5% to $5.29bn; last year had an extra week, and organic growth was 12%.
Adjusted operating income rose 15% to $331m, but about $26m of extra incentive pay cut adjusted EPS by $0.07 to $0.71.
Full year: revenue up 9% to $20.1bn, adjusted EPS up 21% to $2.23 and record free cash flow of $573m.
Record new business wins of $1.9bn and client retention of about 97%; net new business was 6.8% of revenue.
New $1bn share buyback replaces the old $500m plan; quarterly dividend raised 17% to $0.14.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027: organic revenue growth of 9–10%, adjusted operating income up 15–19% and adjusted EPS up 20–25% (constant currency, before buybacks), with leverage at or below 2.7x.

points: The FY27 plan assumes base business growth of 3–4% (about 3% pricing) plus about 6% from net new business.
Aramark Nexus, the remote-site and data center housing unit, added about 1% to Q4 growth; about $500m of FY27 revenue is expected from it.
Margins are planned to widen by 30–40 basis points, with free cash flow conversion falling back to about 40% of operating profit.
The new $1bn buyback is to be used over several years; reinvesting in the business stays the first priority.
Risks flagged: data center permitting pace, a possible baseball labour dispute and start-up costs for new college contracts.
